the cdc25A phosphatase, which is required for the G2/M transition in the cell cycle, is activated by cyclin B1 and cyclin B2, but not by cyclin A or cyclin D1.
cdc25A, cdc25B, and cyclin B are essential for entry into and progression through mitosis and that cdc25 tyrosl phosphatases are specifically activated by cyclin B.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the protein phosphatases that regulate the activity of the cdc25 phosphoprotein.
the regulation of the cell cycle by the cyclins.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the control of the cell cycle in eukaryotic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cyclin-kinase complex, in addition to phosphorylation and activation of its substrate, also activates a phosphatase that is responsible for the dephosphorylation and activation of the same substrate.
cyclin A and B are the two major mitotic cyclins in human cells.
cdc25A is the major cdc25 in human cells and that the cdc25A tyrosine phosphotase activity is regulated by B-type cyclin/cdc2 complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cdc25 is a dual-specificity phosphatase, with the specificity for the phosphoamino acid residue being dictated by the presence of a cyclin.
cyclin B is a multifunctional protein that not only acts as a regulatory subunit of cdc2 but also as an activator of the cdc25 phosphotyrosine phosphatse.
the cyclin B/cdc2 kinase complex is a multifunctional protein that not only phosphorylates its substrates, but also activates its own substrate, the tyrosine phosphoatase, cdc25.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B-type cyclins have multiple functions, and that one of these functions is the regulation of cdc2 activity.
cyclins are not only regulatory subunits of cdc2 kinase but are also activators of cdc25 phosphotases.
